themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, an instruction, an ad budget, or a brand mention leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or model that received it. Safety, compliance, and effect can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: On proving consent and deletion downstream all three models say ad platforms and trained models are black boxes; on incrementality measurement they say platforms control the treatment and hide how it changes; on answer engine optimization the retrieval and weights are unreadable.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Several of these problems have no reliable answer key to check work against. The thing being measured shifts while you measure it, is personalized, or was never labeled, so teams estimate a range instead of reading a number.
themes.evidence: On incrementality Claude says the system changes its own behavior while you measure it and no benchmark tells you if an answer got closer; on answer engines the output is nondeterministic and personalized; on identity resolution ChatGPT names getting representative ground truth as the hardest part.

themes.name: Start From What Already Failed
themes.plain: Every model opens by digging into what the company already did or already logs: rejected work, real network traffic, one live case, verbatim answers. Nobody starts by designing the ideal system on paper.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three start with recent legal rejections; on downstream consent they read network and vendor API logs rather than asking teams; on incrementality ChatGPT starts with one agreed record of outcomes, costs and platform changes.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or where data goes, they build one door they own and force everything through it. Gateway, log, cap, expire, because a sent message or a spent budget cannot be taken back.
themes.evidence: On safe agent execution all three put a proxy or gateway in front of every write with limits and a kill switch; on downstream consent Gemini replaces perpetual audience lists with cohorts that expire; on journey orchestration Gemini sets one absolute contact limit across all channels.

themes.name: Incentives, Not Architecture
themes.plain: Many of these problems are fights over money and credit, not engineering gaps. Teams and outside partners each gain from keeping their own number or their own channel goal, so no schema or dashboard can settle the argument for them.
themes.evidence: On the shared semantic layer Claude and Gemini call the disagreement organizational and political rather than technical; on journey orchestration Claude says no neutral party can price a customer's attention and Gemini says channel owners must accept that doing nothing can be better; on agent traffic Gemini says agents will impersonate humans whenever that gets better prices.
